text:
emma (support): Hi team — customer dropped a screen recording but we can't find the reqref in the UI screenshot. Can someone paste step-by-step for extracting the request id / trace from a video?

cara (acct-xyz): here's the link to the vid: https://files.customer.com/recordings/clip123.mp4 (they said the error shows at ~00:14)

maria (support): thanks — quick checklist: 1) give us the exact video timestamp(s) where the failed request appears, 2) export a tiny HAR or copy-as-curl from the devtools if possible, 3) if mobile/webview, grab SDK logs or a debug token.

raj (eng): if they only have the video, tell them to pause the video at the network call frame and follow these browser steps: open DevTools > Network > find the request > right-click > "Copy" > "Copy as cURL" OR "Save all as HAR". Then paste the curl/HAR snippet here or attach the file.

emma (support): Example curl we can run locally (they can replace <AUTH> and <BODY>):

```bash
curl -v 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <AUTH>' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwkv-large","prompt":"hello"}'
```

raj (eng): If the request is proxied or masked by a webview, we often find a parity header `x-rw-req` or `x-rw-session`. Ask the customer to pause the video, hover over headers in the devtools panel and screenshot the headers pane at the same timestamp. A screenshot + timestamp is often enough for us to find the trace in our logs.

maria (support): For mobile webviews: if they can't access devtools, ask for a 10-15s clipped video centered on the event, and include the user-id/username and approximate UTC timestamp (e.g., 2026-03-14T12:14:23Z). We can correlate by time and user.

cara (acct-xyz): done, uploaded a 15s clip clipped_001.mp4 and a screenshot of devtools at 00:14. Also pasted the curl.

support-bot: file uploaded: clipped_001.mp4 (15.2 MB)

raj (eng): Great — next steps for us: (1) run the curl they pasted to reproduce, (2) search our logs for the exact timestamp + user and the `x-rw-req` header value, (3) if missing, ask them to share a HAR export — HAR contains full request/response timing and headers which is best.

emma (support): Reminder to the customer: redact any PII from HAR before sending. If they can't redact, we can provide a temporary secure upload link and our privacy note.

maria (support): If they give only the video and no headers, we can still try a time-and-user correlation but it takes longer. Ask for these three minimal items to speed up: video timestamp, username/account id, short HAR or "copy as curl" text.

raj (eng): If we reproduce an auth 401 or 403, include the full response body (screenshots are ok). For latency issues include the network waterfall screenshot or HAR — we look at blocking, dns, ssl, and time-to-first-byte.

emma (support): Thanks — I'll message the customer these specific asks and request the upload link if they prefer a private transfer.

cara (acct-xyz): thanks! attaching the HAR now: network_capture.har

support-bot: file uploaded: network_capture.har (1.1 MB)

raj (eng): Perfect — I'll pick this up and follow up in-thread with repro steps or escalate if we need deeper traces. :thumbsup:
